Question: Do you know why I'm only getting 1.6GB/s down and up on WiFi 7 speeds on the Samsung S24 Ultra? On wired, I get a full 3 GB/s.
Answer: As an evolution of 802.11, Wi-Fi 7 is still a shared medium, half-duplex technology. You can be getting new data down, or you can be sending ACKs for the data that you received, but once the sliding window down fills up, you turn the connection around often enough that the speed goes down to a little better than half. This is because ACKs are smaller than actual data being shipped down to you.

Question: How does optical-based motion capture software work?
Answer: By comparing groups of pixels against other groups of pixels, with a drift degree, to determine frame content changes. I’ve always called these 3x3 elements “poxels”; the name never caught on. The relative equivalent is when they “face obscure” (it’s not obscure; trust me) by expanding a one pixel in nine or similar to represent the pixls under all pixel elements. So, for example, they’d “blur” people in video on Oprah, talking about sensitive topics, by taking the upper left pixel, and creating a “poxel” from it, and the entire 3x3 area got to look like the one pixel. Only, if you think about it — no one actually thinks — means that it’s a slow scan oversampling, and if you collapse 3 frames to one frame, the image of the “obscured” person comes out, clean as day. Same thing image stabilization cameras do every day,in fact. Viva le resistance!
